target.paper: Four-Coloring P6-Free Graphs. II. Finding an Excellent Precoloring
target.theorem_object: Lemma 11 local representative state Q_{T,T'} and all downstream consumers before any SPLIT repair
target.question: What is the minimum replacement interface for Q_{T,T'} that could represent a rigid P7 split corridor while leaving Z(Q), admissibility, P_{Q,f'}, soundness/completeness, and polynomial accounting well-defined?

required_outputs.R1_OLD_STATE_INTERFACE: Complete inventory of all definitions, proof obligations, and complexity bounds that consume P,M,N, their membership/adjacency relations, their cardinality pattern, V(Q_{T,T'}), S(Q), Z(T,T'), Z(Q), or Q-admissibility.
required_outputs.R2_NECESSARY_INFORMATION: For each consumed fact classify KEEP, DERIVE, REPLACE, or UNKNOWN. No repair may be proposed as proven.
required_outputs.R3_MINIMAL_NEW_INTERFACE: Specify only the smallest abstract fields/relations required so every old consumer remains formulable. This is a language/interface specification, not an implementation or candidate SPLIT algorithm.
required_outputs.R4_CONSERVATIVE_EMBEDDING: Give a canonical embedding obligation for all three legacy patterns (0,0,0), (0,0,1), (1,1,1), proving that legacy support, Z-semantics, admissible functions, constructed normal subcase, and counting semantics are unchanged under the embedding.

forbidden: define a concrete SPLIT transition system
audit_discipline: Bind every interface item to the primary source.
Distinguish semantic consumers from complexity/accounting consumers.
Do not treat Z(T,T')=empty in the legacy (1,1,1) case as automatically valid for a future split mode.
Do not assume two split witnesses are both added to S(Q); record that as UNKNOWN unless forced by a consumer.
Do not alter the original COMMON case when defining conservative embedding.
STOP after R1-R4 and an explicit list of unresolved obligations.
